summary.intent: Continue development of the monokl code-search tool: add a held-out question set to the rg-compare harness to check that ranking improvements generalize, and move the open PRs (Rust analyzer, language filter, ADR, held-out set) toward merge.
summary.outcome: A subagent opened PR #81 with held-out questions (23/24 questions, 12/12 members) and the tuned scores were unchanged. #77 (Rust analyzer) conflicted with main, so an agent was dispatched to merge main into it; no PRs had merged yet and the bounded-work PRs remain blocked.

repo: rg-compare.repos marks a repo as `held-out` to exclude it from identifier sampling; its question rows carry a `held_out` cell, and a policy note sits at the top of rg-compare.questions.
Held-out policy: misses are never fixed by editing the question; the held-out set is a regression guard, not a tuning target.
Both new held-out gate flags default to 0, and the plan is to raise them to the measured numbers after #81 merges, as was done for the tuned gates.
bench.py loads rg-compare.py's mirrored `is_test_path` and skips test paths when sampling identifiers.
Baseline scores to preserve: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, and Rust fd rows 0/24 (no Rust analyzer on main until #77 merges).
date-fns has no member rows because it has no classes.

The pipeline has a parallel per-file fold that must produce output identical to the serial order; #77 touches `owned_hits`, `retrieve_blocks`, test blocks and the empty-result hint, which overlap with #74, #75 and #76 that merged to main.
Verification checks used: `just ci` and `python3 -I scripts/rg-compare.py`, judged by exit code.

code.finding: Modified while resolving merge conflicts for #77 against main; conflicts came from the changes in #74-#76 to the same pipeline code. Specific line numbers are not given in the transcript.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions; the assistant summarized them without treating them as approval.
Resolve PR conflicts with a merge commit (no rebase or force push) and prove equivalence by comparing old-main and merged release binaries byte for byte on 40+ queries.
Held-out evaluation sets should be written and rg-verified before the first run of the tool under test.
The small held-out set (24 + 12 rows) is coarse, since one miss moves the score about 4 points.

friction: #77 conflicted with main after #74, #75 and #76 merged underneath it.
Entire Gates on #77, #79, #80 and #81 wait on user approval, so nothing has merged.
The bench.py change was only verified on the zod sampler and not run end to end.
CI on #81 had not finished when reported.
open_items: Merge #77 (Rust analyzer), #79 (language filter), #80 (ADR), #81 (held-out set) and #59 (release PR) once approved.
After #81 merges, raise the held-out gates to the measured numbers.
After #77 and #79 merge, start the bounded-work PRs: fixed parse stack with nesting pre-scan, size-before-read with hit-text cap, `--timeout`, and CI scaling tests.
Run bench.py end to end to validate the test-path skipping change.
Measure the Rust fd rows after the analyzer merge without raising gates.
The trpc 'create websocket client' question misses (createWSClient file at rank 7).
